_howToUpdate: To add a new tax year: copy the newest block under "years", rename its key to the new year, and update the numbers.
Then set "activeYear" to the new year. No code changes are needed.
In any bracket list, "max": null means no upper limit (the top bracket).
Brackets must be contiguous: each bracket's min must equal the previous bracket's max. The planner checks this on load and reports the exact field if something is off.
Filing-status keys: "single" and "married" (married filing jointly) are required. Any status without its own entry falls back to "married".
Medicare premiums and IRMAA tables are NOT in the tax-year blocks: see the top-level "medicare" section, which is keyed by premium year.

ordinaryBrackets._noteQualifyingSurvivingSpouse: Qualifying surviving spouse uses the married (joint) brackets via the fallback.

capitalGainsBrackets._noteQualifyingSurvivingSpouse: Qualifying surviving spouse uses the married (joint) thresholds via the fallback.

agedAdditionalStandardDeduction._note: Added to the standard deduction for each filer (and spouse, if filing jointly) at or above this age. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 sec. 3.14(3). The separate amount for blindness is not modeled.

seniorDeduction._note: OBBBA enhanced deduction for seniors, Schedule 1-A Part V. Applies 2025-2028 only: set this whole entry to null for 2029 and later. Per person = perPerson minus phaseOutRate x (MAGI over threshold), not below zero.

socialSecurityTaxabilityThresholds._noteLivedApart: Pub 915: married filing separately who lived apart from their spouse ALL year use the single base amounts; living together at any time gives a $0 base.

taxpayerCredit._note: Utah taxpayer tax credit (Utah Code 59-10-1018; TC-40 lines 11-20): creditRate x (federal standard deduction incl. the 65+ extra + personalExemption per dependent), reduced by phaseOutRate x Utah taxable income above basePhaseOut. Utah publishes each year's amounts in that year's TC-40 instructions; the 2026 ones were not out yet, so these are the 2025 amounts (amountsYear). Replace them and set amountsYear to 2026 when they are published.

socialSecurityCredit._note: Utah Social Security benefits credit (Utah Code 59-10-1042; TC-40A code AH): flatRate x taxable Social Security benefits, reduced by phaseOutRate x modified AGI above the threshold. The thresholds are fixed in the statute (not indexed); these are the 2025-and-later amounts. Nonrefundable; applied after the taxpayer credit.

retirementCredit._note: Utah retirement credit (Utah Code 59-10-1019; TC-40A code 18): perPerson for each filer (and joint-return spouse) born on or before Dec. 31 of bornOnOrBefore, reduced by phaseOutRate x modified AGI above the threshold. Cannot be combined with the Social Security credit; the planner uses whichever is larger. Amounts from the 2025 TC-40 instructions.

_howToUpdate: Each November CMS publishes the next year's Part B premium and IRMAA table. Add it under premiumYears, keyed by the year the premiums apply to (not the income year).

IRMAA for a tax year's income is set by the table lookbackYears later (2026 income -> 2028 premiums). The planner uses that year's published table if it is here; otherwise it projects the newest published table forward only the missing years, so each November's update shortens the projection.
The growth rates under projection are assumptions: review them each year against the latest published changes.

projection._noteThresholds: Income thresholds are indexed to CPI-U and rounded to the nearest $1,000 (SSA sec. 1839(i)(5)). Default 2.8% = the 2025->2026 change ($106,000 -> $109,000).
projection._noteStatutory: The statutory single-filer dollar amounts every lower threshold is indexed from (sec. 1839(i)(3)(C)); joint thresholds are twice the single ones. Used to reproduce SSA's per-tier rounding when projecting.
projection._noteTop: The top threshold ($500,000 single / $750,000 joint) is fixed by law through this year and indexed to CPI-U from the year after.
projection._noteSurcharges: Surcharges and base premiums follow Medicare costs, not CPI. Defaults: Part B 7.8% = average of the 2025 (+5.9%) and 2026 (+9.7%) Part B premium increases; Part D 6% ~ the 2026 top-tier Part D surcharge increase (+6.1%).

2026._source: CMS fact sheets: 2026 Medicare Parts A & B Premiums and Deductibles; 2026 Part D bid information (Part D base beneficiary premium).
2026._notePremiums: Per-person monthly base premiums before IRMAA. Part D varies by plan: this default is the CMS national base beneficiary premium; replace it with your own plan's premium for a closer estimate.

irmaaBrackets._noteMarriedFilingSeparately: CMS: applies to those who lived with their spouse at any time during the year and file separately. Lived apart all year uses the single table.
